title: Virtue without trying
hookLine: the highest virtue doesn't try to be virtuous, and so has virtue (Tao Te Ching 38)

cards: A paper grocery bag splits on the sidewalk, and oranges roll everywhere. Before anyone has decided anything, a teenager with headphones is already crouched down, chasing one into the gutter. Hands it back, nods, walks on.
No speech. No look-at-me. Ask about it later and there'd probably be a shrug.
By tradition, yesterday's chapter closed the first part of the Tao Te Ching, the part on the Tao.
Chapter thirty-eight opens the second part, with today's word, and it starts with a riddle about exactly that kind of kindness.

teach.h: DE: THE POWER OF BEING IN TUNE.
teach.b: First, the word. De, written 德, is the Te in Tao Te Ching. In English it's given as virtue, but not in the sense of a list of rules.
It's closer to the power or quality something has when it's in tune with the Tao. Second, the riddle.

teach.h: HIGHEST DE DOESN'T TRY TO BE DE.
teach.b: The chapter says the highest de doesn't try to be de, and that's why it has it. The lower kind never lets go of being virtuous, and that's why it falls short.
The teenager with the oranges isn't thinking, I am a kind person. The kindness just happens. The moment it becomes a performance, something thins out.
Third, the ladder down. The chapter traces a slide. When the Tao is lost, de comes after.
When de is lost, benevolence. When benevolence is lost, righteousness. When righteousness is lost, propriety, the rules of proper form.
And propriety, it says, is the thin edge of loyalty and good faith, and the beginning of disorder. Each step is a little more effort and a little less real. Fourth, the fruit.

The chapter ends by saying the great person stays with what is thick, not what is thin, with the fruit and not the flower. Back on the sidewalk, that's the difference between kindness and looking kind.
One is the orange handed back. The other is the post about handing it back. The chapter isn't against good manners.
It's pointing underneath them, to the thing manners were trying to copy.

how: Readers of the Tao Te Ching often take chapter thirty-eight as a warning against goodness as performance, valuing the kindness that comes naturally over rules and appearances.

games.q: a stranger's grocery bag splits on the sidewalk. what does chapter thirty-eight's highest de look like?
o: help, then tell everyone you helped.
help, without stopping to think of yourself as good.
first decide whether helping is the virtuous thing.
games.why: the highest de doesn't try to be de. the lower kind holds on to being virtuous, and so falls short.

practice: If there's a voice in your head that narrates your good deeds, the one that says look, I'm being patient, just notice it. Then let it go quiet, the way a radio fades when you walk out of the room.
Rest a moment in the quiet where it was.

wordCard.voice: De. The Te in Tao Te Ching: virtue, or power, the quality of being in tune with the Tao. The highest de doesn't try to be de. Today's word.
